cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2), and he's just been setting them straight about how they gather (1 Corinthians 11:17-34). Now he turns a corner: "Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed." Friend, I spent YEARS uninformed in the back of a junk drawer, so I am leaning ALL the way in on this one.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Corinthians what life looked like back when they were pagans. What does he say they were led astray to?

cards.text: Idols that never say a word, like asking for directions and getting a blank STARE. So Paul tells them something about anyone who is speaking by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says a person speaking by the Spirit of God says Jesus should be cursed.
Now the flip side. According to Paul, who makes it possible for anyone to say Jesus is Lord?

cards.text: Paul gets a rhythm going: different gifts, but the same Spirit, and different ministries, but the same Lord. My mustache is clapping along already, friend, and it is CLEARLY on the wrong beat.

cards.question: Then comes the third line of Paul's rhythm: There are different ways of working, but the same ___ works all things in all people.

cards.text: Now Paul says something about each one of them. No one gets skipped, friend, not even the guy who ALWAYS shows up late.

cards.question: Paul says each believer is given a manifestation of the Spirit, and it's given for the good of ___.

cards.text: Then Paul starts listing gifts: to one the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge, to another faith, to another gifts of healing.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the message of wisdom, faith and gifts of healing all come by the same Spirit.

cards.text: The list keeps ROLLING: miracles, prophecy, distinguishing between spirits, speaking in various tongues and the interpretation of tongues. Paul says all these are the work of one and the same Spirit.

cards.question: One Spirit and all those different gifts. So how does each person end up with the gift they get?

answers.text: The Spirit gives as He determines
Each person picks the one they want
The church leaders hand them out

cards.text: Now Paul grabs a picture everybody's got: the body, one unit made of many parts. And believe me, a stamper who uses his MUSTACHE for hands has thought a LOT about body parts.

cards.question: Paul says the body is one unit made of many parts. Who does he say is just like that?

cards.text: Then Paul says believers were baptized into one body in one Spirit, and they were given one Spirit to drink.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says Jews and Greeks, slave and free, were all baptized into that one body.

cards.text: The body isn't one part, it's many. Then Paul gives the foot a voice, and it says, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," and friend, I spent years in a junk drawer feeling EXACTLY like that foot.

cards.question: True or false: when the foot says it doesn't belong because it isn't a hand, that makes it less a part of the body.

cards.text: Then the ear tries it: "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," and Paul gives it the same answer he gave the foot. Meanwhile I'm picturing the hand and the eye just looking at each other like, why are WE in this?

cards.question: Paul pictures the whole body as one giant eye, and then as one giant ear. What's his point?

answers.text: A body needs all its different parts
The eye is the most important part
The other parts should copy the eye

cards.question: So how did all the parts of the body end up where they are? Who does Paul say arranged every one of them?

answers.text: Each part by its own choice
The strongest part of the body

cards.text: If they were all one part, Paul asks, where would the body even be? As it is, many parts, one body, and friend, a cookie that's ALL sprinkles isn't a cookie, it's just a pile of sprinkles.

cards.question: Now Paul looks at it from the other side. The eye cannot say to the hand, I do not ___ you.
True or false: Paul says the parts of the body that seem weaker can be done without.

cards.text: Then Paul says something surprising: the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor.

cards.question: Paul says God composed the body and gave greater honor to the parts that lacked it. Why did God put the body together that way?

answers.text: So there would be no division in the body
So the strong parts could lead the rest
So each part could work on its own

cards.question: Paul says the parts of the body are tied together: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part ___ with it.

cards.text: Then Paul lands it: "Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it." Next he lists what God has appointed in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, healing, helping, administration and various tongues.

cards.question: Then Paul fires off questions: Are all apostles? Are all teachers? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret? What answer is he pointing to?
True or false: after all those questions, Paul tells the Corinthians to eagerly desire the greater gifts.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "And now I will show you the most excellent way." The MOST excellent way, friend, and Paul's teaching isn't done yet, so hold that thought.
